cat_and_fiddle_inn_0.text: Welcome to the Cat and Fiddle. The second highest inn in England, at about 1,690 feet. The wind is included.
It was built about two hundred years ago beside the old road between Macclesfield and Buxton. Folk have argued about the name ever since.
Some say it comes from a French phrase, Caton Fidele. Others from the nursery rhyme. I say the cat is sensible and the fiddler is loud.

cat_and_fiddle_inn_1.text: I came up for the wind and the view. Both are generous. Keep an ear out for hootlets at dusk.
